questiontext.text: Given keys with known search frequencies, what does the Optimal BST algorithm minimize?

feedback.text: Correct — it minimizes the frequency-weighted total depth of searches.
No — minimizing height ignores the frequencies; a balanced tree is not always optimal here.
No — the node count is fixed by the key set.
No — the objective is expected search cost, not edge length.

generalfeedback.text: OBST arranges keys so that the sum over all keys of (frequency × depth) is minimized — the expected search cost.

questiontext.text: Which algorithmic technique is used to construct an Optimal BST?

feedback.text: Correct — it builds solutions for larger key ranges from optimal sub-ranges.
No — unlike Huffman, a greedy root choice does not yield the optimum.
No — naive recursion recomputes overlapping subproblems; DP tables are needed.
No — the standard solution is dynamic programming.

generalfeedback.text: OBST is a classic dynamic programming problem: the optimal tree over a key range combines optimal subtrees over sub-ranges.

questiontext.text: What is the time complexity of the standard dynamic programming Optimal BST algorithm for n keys?

feedback.text: Correct — O(n^2) subproblems, each trying O(n) possible roots.
No — that is too fast; the DP fills an O(n^2) table with an inner root loop.
No — DP avoids the exponential blow-up of trying every tree shape.
No — a single pass cannot solve OBST.

generalfeedback.text: There are O(n^2) key-range subproblems and each tries O(n) roots, giving O(n^3); Knuth's optimization reduces it to O(n^2).

questiontext.text: In an Optimal BST, keys that are searched more frequently tend to be placed:

feedback.text: Correct — shallower depth for frequent keys lowers the expected cost.
No — that would raise their access cost.
No — position depends on key order and frequencies, not a fixed slot.
No — placement follows BST ordering and cost, not a fixed side.

generalfeedback.text: Because cost = frequency × depth, high-frequency keys are pushed toward the root to reduce their depth.

questiontext.text: An Optimal BST is always the same as a perfectly height-balanced BST.

feedback.text: No — when frequencies are skewed, an unbalanced tree can have lower expected cost.
Correct — optimality depends on frequencies, not just on balance.

questiontext.text: An Optimal BST must still satisfy the binary-search-tree ordering property on its keys.

feedback.text: Correct — it is a BST, so in-order traversal yields the keys in sorted order.
It is still a BST; only the shape is chosen to minimize cost.

questiontext.text: The Optimal BST is solved by ______ programming (fill in the one-word technique name).

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about Optimal BST construction are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: It uses a dynamic programming table over ranges of consecutive keys

feedback.text: Yes — subproblems are contiguous key ranges.

answer.text: It minimizes expected search cost using the key frequencies

feedback.text: Yes — frequencies drive the objective.

answer.text: It is a greedy algorithm like Huffman coding

feedback.text: No — OBST needs DP; a greedy root choice is not optimal.

answer.text: It ignores search frequencies and only balances the tree

feedback.text: No — frequencies are central to the objective.

generalfeedback.text: OBST: dynamic programming over key ranges, minimizing frequency-weighted expected cost; it is not greedy and does not ignore frequencies.
